title: refactor(ci): consolidate lint/test/release workflows and optimize cache/parallelism
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Our CI workflows have diverged over time resulting in duplicated matrix definitions, inconsistent caching (different keys for JS/Python steps), and slow runner utilization for PRs touching multiple packages. This PR consolidates lint/test/release into a smaller set of reusable workflows, standardizes cache keys and retention, and adds controlled job parallelism to reduce wall-clock time. Summary of changes: - Split the previous three workflows into two consolidated workflows: .github/workflows/ci-lint-test.yml (lint + unit/integration tests) and .github/workflows/release.yml (release automation + tagging). - Extracted common workflow logic into reusable workflow templates and a small actions/ helper (github/actions/cache-helpers) for deterministic cache keys across languages. - Introduced test-matrix packing strategy: run fast unit suites across lightweight runners in parallel, and run heavier integration suites on a reduced matrix. - Improved cache keys to include OS, node/python version, and a repository-path-specific sha segment to avoid cross-package cache corruption. - Added optional parallel test sharding script scripts/ci/parallelize-tests.sh that is feature-flagged to preserve current behavior for top-tier repos. - Updated docs/docs/ci/README.md with migration notes and rollback guidance. Checklist: - [x] re-useable workflow templates created - [x] cache key deterministic across JS/Python - [x] test matrix validated on canary repo - [x] release workflow linted and dry-run tested - [x] updated CI quotas and runner labels negotiated with infra Migration notes: CI consumers should switch from old workflow refs to the new consolidated workflow via examples in docs/ci/README.md. If you rely on bespoke runner labels, ensure label mapping in the repo-level ci config. Rollback: revert to branch ci/rollback/350123 (keeps previous workflows intact) for immediate fallback.

review_conversation: Evan Liu (reviewer): Can we avoid introducing a global cache key that could cause cross-package pollution? Suggest adding repo path and a short commit sha — done in second commit.

Diego Morales (reviewer): The parallelize script looks promising but could destabilize flaky tests. Suggest feature-flagging and conservative shard counts. Author updated script to be opt-in and added a SHARD_COUNT env var.
Priya Singh (reviewer): Please pin GH action versions for security/hygiene — addressed in commit e5a6b7c.
Evan Liu (approver): Verified canary run on redwood-examples, CI duration reduced ~28% for PRs touching multiple packages. Approving.
